entries.title: Literally everyone hated this feature
entries.summary: Meta launched Muse Image, an AI image-generation feature that by default let anyone @-mention a public account and generate new AI images of that person's likeness without consent. After backlash from users, privacy advocates, and talent agencies, Meta pulled the feature just three days after launch.

entries.title: CLAUDE FORGETS EVERYTHING. THESE TWO FIX IT
entries.summary: The video pairs two free, open-source Claude Code skills to fix Claude's lack of memory: research-skill gives Claude a persistent, project-scoped research memory that survives context wipes, while claude-deep-research-skill turns Claude into an 8-phase deep-research agent with source credibility scoring.

entries.title: Claude demonstrates deep internet data removal and ongoing #ClaudeAI #dataprivacy #infosecurity
entries.summary: The video claims Claude Co-Work can automatically find personal data exposed on data-broker/people-search sites and submit removal requests. A top comment disputes this, saying Claude itself states it cannot produce a definitive exposure list for sites like Spokeo or WhitePages, calling the demo likely fabricated — treat the claim as unverified.

entries.title: 4 Ways to Stop Wasting Tokens with AI
entries.summary: The video explains that Claude's token cost compounds with conversation length because every reply re-reads the whole thread, and gives four concrete fixes: Clear to reset history to zero, Compact to shrink it, disconnecting unused MCP servers (which cost context even idle), and Rewind to delete a wrong turn instead of arguing with the model.

entries.title: AI Smells Fishy? Experts Doubt Cyber Eval Claims #shorts
entries.summary: The video reports a disputed cybersecurity eval claim: an American AI model was allegedly compromised, was blocked by its own guardrails, and the response involved switching to Chinese open-source models to defend against another American AI. Experts quoted are skeptical it was a real attack rather than benchmark overfitting; no specific model names are given.
